answer: Let every newcomer defend its history at a summit: it must first publish a sonnet — fourteen fixed lines, each a checkable claim about one real job, client, and outcome — then face live questioning from interrogators drawn by yarrow-stalk lots, so no farmer can predict or bribe its probers. Every answer is recorded and checked against the sonnet and earlier answers; one contradiction burns the identity and pays the catcher. Forging a thousand faces means writing a thousand consistent sonnets and surviving a thousand hostile examinations by examiners chosen by chance and paid to catch lies.
